sections.history: Thiruvallikeni, today's Triplicane, lies beside the Marina in Chennai, and its temple is one of the 108 Divya Desams, the abodes of Vishnu sung by the Alvars in the Nalayira Divya Prabandham. It belongs to Thondai Nadu, and three Alvars — Peyalvar, Thirumazhisai Alvar and Thirumangai Alvar — sang of the Lord here. The foundation is attributed to the Pallavas; accounts place the present temple in the eighth century, and an inscription of the Pallava king Dantivarman, who reigned into the ninth century, is preserved within it. Thirumangai Alvar's hymn describes the temple as it stood in Pallava times. One account dates the present shrine of Vedavalli Thayar to the later nineteenth century.
sections.architecture: The temple is approached from Car Street, the broad processional avenue that gives the quarter its character. Opposite the east entrance lies the Kairavini Pushkarini, the temple tank named for the kairavini, the lily, and said to contain five wells. Within the complex stand separate shrines for Vedavalli Thayar, Yoga Narasimha, Rama, Gajendra Varadaraja and Ranganatha, so that five forms of Vishnu are worshipped in one place. The Thayar's shrine runs parallel to the sanctum of the presiding Lord.
sections.legends: The Lord here is Parthasarathy, Krishna as the charioteer of Partha, or Arjuna, on the field of Kurukshetra. He is shown with a moustache, a rarity among images of Vishnu, and tradition holds that he carries only the conch, having raised no weapon in the war. The face of the processional image is said to bear the marks of arrows from that battle. Devotees come to the teacher of the Gita as he stands patiently among the houses of the city.
sections.festivals: The Chithirai Brahmotsavam is the great festival, and the temple car runs twice — once for Parthasarathy and once for Yoga Narasimha. The Masi Theppam, the float festival, carries the Lord across the Kairavini tank, and Vaikunta Ekadashi draws large crowds. Confirm dates locally.
sections.experience: A living city temple in the heart of Chennai, easily joined with a walk to the Marina. Take time to visit the several shrines in turn — Thayar, Yoga Narasimha, Rama, Varadaraja and Ranganatha — and to see the Kairavini tank opposite the east entrance. Festival days are crowded, so allow extra time.

visit.timings: Open daily with morning and evening darshan sessions and a midday closure; festival days and Vaikunta Ekadashi are busiest. Confirm current timings before visiting.
visit.dressCode: Modest traditional dress is expected — shoulders and knees covered; footwear removed before entering. Follow the posted rules and the priests' guidance.
visit.photography: Photography is restricted in and around the sanctum; follow the posted rules and the priests' guidance.
visit.gettingThere: In Triplicane, central Chennai, on Car Street near the Marina; reached by city road from Chennai Central and Egmore stations. Chennai International Airport is the nearest airport.
